title: Fold a pop-up laundry hamper
instruction: Twist-fold the pop-up laundry hamper and secure it with its retaining loop.
setup: An empty, ordinary 33 x 33 x 53 cm spring-steel and polyester-mesh laundry hamper, flattened into its full 33 x 53 cm rectangle but not twisted or coiled. Its attached elastic retaining loop lies loose beside it. The flat hamper lies on a 350 x 380 x 100 mm open wooden rest with a 10 mm base and two 20 mm-wide, 90 mm-high rails, 330 mm centre-to-centre on the table with the 53 cm length between the arms and the 33 cm width running forward. Both hands start open, with 2 x 18 x 24 mm silicone finger-pad covers. No latch or fixture holds a folded shape.
scoring: 1.0 if the hamper forms a packet no larger than 22 x 22 x 6 cm, its retaining loop surrounds it, and it remains within those dimensions for three seconds after both hands release. 0.5 for the same compact packet while held or unsecured; 0.25 for a packet no larger than 35 x 25 cm. Otherwise 0. A broken frame, detached loop or torn fabric scores 0. Use a ruler and the released video.
fidelity: Flattened layers use one aggregate spring frame and a hinged cloth net; inter-layer slip and mesh shear resistance are omitted. Cloth collision is sampled at nodes and links. Slender-body inertia is regularized. Fixed rest angles, native contact and spring-back produce the fold. Silicone-pad proxies and a 40 N/finger ceiling apply to both runs. Materials are uncalibrated; no commanded collapse or hand attachment. Full validation is pending.
scores: Development demos: 0.0; Dream not yet run. Not submission-ready.
context: A pop-up hamper must be twisted into nested loops and restrained before its spring frame opens again.
reset_notes: Use a full-size pop-up mesh hamper with an attached elastic retaining loop, such as the 13 x 13 x 21 inch Smart Design type. Open it, inspect the wire and seams, flatten the sides without twisting the frame, then restore the photographed rectangle and loose loop. Do not start from an already coiled frame.
